subject.title: Workboard: improve stacked-card readability and human-approval visibility

question: Should Workboard represent human-approval/action-required cards as a first-class UI concept, a configurable prominent-label rule, or leave this to existing status and label conventions?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the durable product contract is not: the fix could be UI-local, metadata-driven, or a new plugin config surface, and repository policy sets a high bar for new config/default behavior.

options.title: Add UI-local human-action signal
options.body: Use existing Workboard status, metadata, notes, or labels to surface a built-in attention count or affordance without creating new plugin config unless later proven necessary.

options.title: Add configurable prominent labels
options.body: Define a plugin-owned config contract for label patterns such as approval-needed, with docs and tests for the new user-visible config surface.

options.title: Keep current conventions
options.body: Defer first-class human-action UX and document blocked status, labels, and filters as the supported workflow.

recommendation.title: Add UI-local human-action signal
recommendation.body: Use existing Workboard status, metadata, notes, or labels to surface a built-in attention count or affordance without creating new plugin config unless later proven necessary.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the Workboard plugin and dashboard surface and is the strongest history-backed owner for this product-surface choice.
